description: next/ v4 — PHASE-0 ARCHITECTURE FIX: REAL ERP OperationsResponse (Level-3 IST/actual feedback) via the sim-v5 ERP REST API (http://192.168.178.154:38260/api/confirmations), replacing the postgresql/erp-operations-response.json direct-erpdb poller (erpdb.llm_test_v3.order_confirmations — the forbidden direct-DB bypass). Same sourceId (edge SOURCE_IDS unchanged), same profile contract (SMProfile-OperationsResponse). production_order_no = join key (cross-rule join + kgIdProperty; RESPONDS_TO ProductionOrder on the same key). confirmed_qty -> quantity_produced drives the qty_shortfall cross-rule against ProductionOrder.qty_planned. cycle_time_actual -> cycle_time_actual_sec (the real actual cycle time). ts_end -> actual_end_time + completed_at (the REST confirmation's end timestamp is the actual completion time; the old postgres source used confirmation_time for both). recorded_at -> updated_at. /api/confirmations has NO status column, but every confirmation IS a completion -> status bound to the constant 'fertig' ({ const: 'fertig', smAttribute: 'status' }) so the OperationsResponse contract is complete. NOTE 2026-07-12: the three cross-rules that gated on this attribute (qty_shortfall, material_unavailable, late_delivery) are RETIRED — a when-guard over a source-bound constant can never discriminate (see their tombstones and ci/lint-cross-constraints.mjs, which fails the build on any ACTIVE rule with such a guard). The constant stays for contract completeness; it MUST NOT be used as a when-guard operand. full_refresh change-detection (the REST API does not honour ?since — verified) — it-edge dedups via the per-id HWM on production_order_no. filter=null (full confirmation set per the cutover decision). machine_no/machine_id are null on the current confirmation feed (BDE bridge does not stamp the machine) — mapped for forward-compat; the ON_MACHINE edge resolves once the feed carries it. scrap_qty/good_qty/operator_id unmapped (not in the profile contract). --- 2026-08-03, THE status CONSTANT IS REMOVED. It bound every OperationsResponse to the literal 'fertig' and therefore asserted, on every record, that the operation was COMPLETE. MEASURED live: 34715 operations_response events reached central-ts in three hours and ALL of them carried status='fertig'. That is a false statement at scale, not a harmless placeholder. I LOOKED FOR A REAL FIELD TO DERIVE IT FROM AND THERE IS NONE. /api/confirmations carries no status column (0 of 5000 rows). The only candidate was final_confirmation, and it is a CONSTANT TOO: measured over the COMPLETE prod population, logistics.bde_confirmations holds 2,038,771 rows and final_confirmation is false on every single one — never true, not once. The `shift` column is NULL on all 2,038,772. So a valueMap would have swapped one constant for another while looking like a derivation. THE ATTRIBUTE IS NOW ABSENT, WHICH IS THE HONEST OUTCOME: a consumer reads no status and reports none, exactly as mappings/machine-identity.json allows erpMachineRef:null so a consumer greys instead of guessing. Absent is not the same class of error as wrong. THE ROOT CAUSE IS UPSTREAM AND IS NOT FIXED HERE: a BDE system in which no confirmation is EVER final never reports an operation complete — the same family as production orders that never go terminal. Deciding WHEN a confirmation becomes final (last operation? planned qty reached? order terminal?) is a modelling choice for sim-v5, not something this descriptor may improvise. When it lands, bind status to final_confirmation via valueMap and EXTEND the profile enum against a paginated measurement.
